text.p: Italian debt futures tested the upper end of the recent range, trading nearly a point higher by the close of business, while the Italian cash market struggled to play catch-up after a day's holiday.
"We've had a correction from a sharp fall in a thin market on Friday," a senior broker at an Italian bank in London said.
Comments by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl at the weekend on being committed to a stable euro launched on time had helped European debt markets in general, the broker said.
In addition a correction by the dollar had helped calm some speculation of a possible German interest rate rise soon.
The July 2007 cash Btp closed five basis points down at 101.17, yielding 6.68 percent and with the spread over the benchmark German Bund at 105 basis points.

The September Btp futures contract on LIFFE was 92 basis points up from Friday's levels at 135.57, with the bottom of the range plotted at 134.70 and the top up around 136.20. Nearby resistance was at 135.65, brokers said.

Brokers said interest rates are the talk of the town, with the Fed's policy-making FOMC meeting on Tuesday to discuss U.S. monetary policy, the Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday and speculation over the prospects for a higher German repo rate.
Beyond those international events, domestic calendar points include preliminary Italian inflation data for August due for release by 11 sample cities on Thursday and Friday.
